issues.legal_issue: A plaint cannot be returned at the preliminary stage on the basis of a disputed claim for post-termination damages when deciding the claim would require prejudging an issue for trial and the claim is not palpably absurd or shown to be made in bad faith.
material_facts: The landlord sued for possession, rent arrears, and damages for the tenant’s continued possession after termination of the tenancy, valuing the suit above the threshold for the High Court’s jurisdiction.
The tenant argued that the landlord could recover only rent at the contractual rate after termination, which would reduce the suit’s valuation below that threshold.
Before trial, the High Court accepted the tenant’s argument, rejected the claimed damages for valuation purposes, and returned the plaint to be filed in another court.
The damages claim was neither palpably absurd nor imaginary, and whether the landlord was entitled to those damages required judicial consideration at trial.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred by prejudging the disputed entitlement to damages and returning the plaint before trial. Its order was set aside, and it was directed to proceed with the suit, deciding the damages issue afresh at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a suit should be instituted in the lowest-grade court competent to try it. Under Order 7, rule 10, a plaint may be returned at any stage for presentation to the proper court. Ordinarily, valuation depends on the relief claimed, although a court may prevent abuse through gross overvaluation or undervaluation. A disputed claim that is not palpably absurd or shown to be made in bad faith should not be rejected for jurisdictional valuation by deciding its merits at a preliminary stage; its entitlement is for determination with the other issues at trial. The judgment names no earlier cases as authorities relied on by the Court.

rule.if: suit_seeks_possession_and_money and pretrial_application_seeks_return_of_plaint and plaintiff_claims_damages_for_continued_possession and damages_entitlement_requires_trial and damages_claim_not_pal pably_absurd

predicates.suit_seeks_possession_and_money: The claimant brought a suit seeking possession of property and monetary relief.
predicates.pretrial_application_seeks_return_of_pla: A party asked the court, before trial, to return the plaint for filing in another court.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_damages_for_continued_p: The claimant sought damages on the basis that the opposing party continued to possess the property after the claimant asserted a right to possession.
predicates.damages_entitlement_requires_trial: Whether the claimant is entitled to the claimed damages depends on an issue that requires judicial determination at trial.
predicates.damages_claim_not_pal pably_absurd: The damages claim is not plainly absurd or imaginary.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks possession and money, a pretrial request to return the plaint cannot be granted on the basis of a damages claim for continued possession if entitlement to those damages requires trial and the claim is not plainly absurd.
